comment: No source is published. The panel is the clearest of the three and it carries one plain error. Over the first knob of each row it prints 66% 3A and over the second 33% 3B, but the code draws a uniform number from 0 to 99 and takes the FIRST knob only when that number is above 65, so the first knob is chosen about 34 per cent of the time and the second about 66. The draw was simulated against the module's own linear congruential generator to confirm the value is uniform over 0 to 99. The third knob of each row, printed Floor, is the voltage that output holds while the clock is low; in the Pool mode there is no floor at all and the output instead latches one of the row's three knobs picked at random, which is what the panel's Latch marking means. The Mode switch is configured as Pool, Bar and Disco at values 0, 1 and 2; the panel prints no names, only the three probability sets, and they match the code in that order: Pool 99, 75 and 40 per cent, Bar 33 per cent for all three rows, Disco 90, 69 and 42. The fourth output, printed Doorman 2%, fires on a separate xorshift generator whose value falls below 1310 out of 65536, which is 2.0 per cent. Reset copies a stored counter back into the random seed and Rnd trig advances that counter, which is how the maker's loopable random gates work. The output named 1A or 2B in configOutput is printed 1A or 1B on the panel. Knob values are scaled 0 to 8V on Unipolar and -8V to +8V on Bipolar.
